Now when the Greeks heard that Diogenes had been captured,
they appointed Michael, the son of Constantine, king over themselves.
And he seized his mother,
who was Diogenes' wife,
and forced her into a monastery.
And his uncle John became Caesar.
Now when Diogenes entered the territory of the Romans
and heard what had happened,
he went up to the fortress of Doukeia {OCR?: Dokia},
and found in it two hundred thousand dinars;
and he sent them to the Sultan, together with those two emirs who had gone with him,
and informed him of the matter.
And he put on the monastic habit,
and stayed in Doukeia {OCR?: Dokia}.
And he sent to Michael, saying:
"I have fought the good fight until now on behalf of the repentance {OCR?: safety/benefit?} of the Christians,
and it is enough for me.
As for you, blessed is your kingdom,
and you have done well to reign,
because it was rightful for you.
Only, faithfully I advise you not to violate the peace that I made with the Sultan;
otherwise, no rest will remain,
neither for you
nor for the Christians {OCR?: ܓܟܪ̈ܣܛܝܢܐ for ܠܟܪ̈ܣܛܝܢܐ}."
And Michael thanked him and said:
"I will not depart from your counsel."
But after some days, certain people incited him,
and he sent to Diogenes, saying to him:
"If in truth you are a monk,
why do you dwell in a fortress? It is right that you go down to one of the monasteries,
so that we may send guards into the fortress."
Diogenes, however, became enraged and said:
"Out of the whole empire of the Romans, he does not even leave me one fortress!"
And he arose and stripped off the woolen garments,
and took the merchandise {OCR?: pledged goods/deposits} of the merchants of Doukeia by way of a loan,
and gathered an army for himself.
And when the son of Sennacherib, the patrician of Armenia Minor, came to him,
he seized him and blinded his eyes,
and took eighty hundredweights (qintars) of gold from him.
And he grew very strong, and came to Melitene,
and sent to Sultan Alp Arslan,
and sought help from him.
And the Sultan promised him
that he himself would go in person to help him wherever occasion demanded.
And after these things,
Diogenes moved from Melitene to Cilicia {OCR?: ܓܩܝܠܝܩܝܐ for ܠܩܝܠܝܩܝܐ}.
And John came against him,
and besieged him in the city of Adana.
And when he captured him,
he sent word and informed King Michael.
